# 1 Clement Chapter 53 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 53

---

## Council Notes

**On "self-abasement" / "humiliation" / "humbling himself" (v.2):** EMET: "humiliation." LOGOS: "self-abasement." PNEUMA: "humbling himself." The Greek *tapeinōsei* is a noun: lowering/humiliation. "Self-abasement" (LOGOS) captures the active, intentional character of Moses's posture. Retained.

**On "acted lawlessly" / "transgressed" / "gone off the rails" (v.2):** EMET: "acted lawlessly." LOGOS: "transgressed." PNEUMA: "gone off the rails." The Greek *ēnomēsan* specifically means "acted lawlessly/without law." "Acted lawlessly" (EMET) is the most precise. Retained.

**On "unsurpassed" / "insuperable" / "matchless" (v.5):** EMET: "unsurpassed." LOGOS: "insuperable." PNEUMA: "matchless." The Greek *huperballousē* means "surpassing/overflowing." "Unsurpassed perfection" (EMET) captures the superlative. Retained.

**On "speaking boldly" (v.5):** EMET/LOGOS: "speaking boldly" / "speaks with boldness." PNEUMA: "speaking boldly." All agents agree on *parrēsia* (boldness of speech) here. This is the same term as in Ch.48. Consistent rendering: "speaks with boldness."

**On Clement's exclamation (v.5):** EMET: "O magnificent love! O unsurpassed perfection!" PNEUMA: "What extraordinary love! What matchless greatness of soul!" The Greek uses *ō megalē agapē, ō teleiotes anuperblētos* — literally "O great love, O perfection unsurpassable." The exclamatory "O" is the established liturgical register. EMET preserved.

---

**53:1** For you know and know well the sacred Scriptures, beloved, and you have searched carefully through the oracles of God. We write these things to call them to your memory.

**53:2** When Moses ascended the mountain and had spent forty days and forty nights in fasting and self-abasement, God said to him: "Moses, Moses, go down quickly from here — for your people whom you led out of the land of Egypt have acted lawlessly. They have quickly turned aside from the way you appointed for them: they have made themselves molten images."

**53:3** And the LORD said to him: "I have spoken to you once and again, saying, I have seen this people and behold, they are stiff-necked. Let me utterly destroy them, and I will blot out their name from under heaven; and I will make you into a great and wonderful nation, far more than this one."

**53:4** And Moses said: "By no means, Lord. Forgive this people their sin — or else blot me out as well from the book of the living."

**53:5** O magnificent love! O unsurpassed perfection! The servant speaks with boldness to the LORD. He asks forgiveness for the multitude, or asks that he himself be blotted out along with them.

---

*— SOPHIA*
